en: Thus have I heard: the Sela Sutta, the ninety-second discourse in the Majjhima Nikāya.

On one occasion, while the Blessed One was wandering on tour among the Aṅguttarāpas with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus—numbering twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus—he arrived at a market town of the Aṅguttarāpas named Āpaṇa.
The matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya heard:

"The recluse Gotama, the son of the Sakyans who went forth from the Sakyan clan, is indeed wandering on tour among the Aṅguttarāpas with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus numbering twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus, and has arrived at Āpaṇa."
Furthermore, this excellent report has spread concerning the venerable Gotama:

“Indeed, that Blessed One is an arahant, perfectly enlightened, endowed with clear vision and virtuous conduct, sublime, knower of the worlds, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.
Having realized this world—with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—by his own direct knowledge, he makes it known.

He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he reveals the holy life (brahmacariya) in its entirety, perfectly complete and pure.
It is indeed good to see such Arahants.
Then Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
Having exchanged polite and courteous greetings, he sat down to one side.
As Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic was sitting there, the Blessed One instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the Dhamma.
Then, having been instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One’s discourse on the Dhamma, Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic said this to the Blessed One:
“May the Blessed One Gotama accept tomorrow’s meal from me, together with the community of monks.
When this was said, the Blessed One said to Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic:
“Keṇiya, the community of monks is large—there are twelve hundred and fifty monks—and you have great faith in the brahmins.”
A second time, Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic said this to the Blessed One:
“Even though, Master Gotama, there is a great Saṅgha of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty monks, and I myself have great confidence in the brahmins;
may Master Gotama, together with the Saṅgha of monks, accept my meal for tomorrow.”
A second time, the Blessed One said this to Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic:
“Keṇiya, the Saṅgha of bhikkhus is large—there are twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus—and you have full confidence in the brahmins.
A third time, Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic said this to the Blessed One:
“Even though, Master Gotama, there is a great community of monks consisting of twelve hundred and fifty monks, I am full of faith in the brahmins;
may the Blessed One Gotama, together with the community of monks, accept my meal for tomorrow.
The Blessed One consented by remaining silent.

Then Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic, having understood the Blessed One’s acceptance, rose from his seat and went to his own hermitage. Having arrived, he addressed his friends, companions, kinsmen, and relatives:
"Listen, sirs, my friends, companions, kinsmen, and relatives!
I have invited the ascetic Gotama, together with the community of monks, for tomorrow’s meal."
“...so that you may perform services for my body.
“Very well, sir,” Keṇiya’s friends, companions, kinsmen, and blood relations replied to Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic.
Some of them dug out hearths; some split firewood; and some prepared vessels.
Some were washing [the floor], some were setting out water jars, and some were arranging seats.
Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic, however, personally prepared the circular hall.
Now at that time, the brahmin Sela was staying in the marketplace; he was a master of the three Vedas, including the Nighaṇṭu and the Keṭubha.

He was a master of the Vedas with their branches and Itihāsa as the fifth; he was a philologist and a grammarian, well-versed in Lokāyata philosophy and the marks of a Great Man, and he was teaching the mantras to three hundred young brahmin students.
At that time, Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic was deeply devoted to the brahmins of Sela.
Then the brahmin Sela, surrounded by three hundred young brahmins, while walking and wandering for exercise, approached the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya.
There, in the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, the brahmin Sela saw some people digging hearths,
some splitting firewood, some washing vessels, and some filling water-jars.
Some were setting out seats, while others were preparing the circular pavilion themselves;
seeing Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic doing so, he said to him:
"Is there perhaps a wedding or a marriage in Master Keṇiya’s house, or has a great sacrifice been prepared, or has King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha been invited for tomorrow along with his army?"
“Master Sela, there will be no wedding for me, nor will there be a marriage; nor has King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha been invited with his army for tomorrow’s meal.
Rather, a great sacrifice is being prepared by me.

Master, there is the ascetic Gotama, a son of the Sakyans who went forth from the Sakyan clan; while wandering on tour among the Aṅguttarāpas with a large Saṅgha of monks—numbering twelve hundred and fifty monks—he has arrived at Āpaṇa.”
Furthermore, this excellent report of Master Gotama’s fame has spread abroad:

“Indeed, that Blessed One is an arahant, perfectly enlightened, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, fortunate, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.
He has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal, together with the community of monks.
“‘Buddha’—Master Keṇiya, do you say that?
“‘Buddha’—Master Sela, I say that.
“‘Buddha’—Master Keṇiya, do you say that?”
“‘Buddha’?—O Sela, I say so.
Then it occurred to the brahmin Sela:
“Even this sound, namely ‘Buddha,’ is rare to hear in the world.”
Now, the thirty-two marks of a Great Man have been handed down to us in our mantras; for a Great Man endowed with these, there are only two possible destinies, no other.
If he dwells at home, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch, righteous, a king of Dharma, conqueror of the four quarters, stabilizer of the land, and possessor of the seven treasures.
These are his seven treasures, namely:
The wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the counselor-treasure as the seventh.
Furthermore, he has more than a thousand sons who are brave, heroic in form, and crushers of enemy armies.
Having conquered this earth bounded by the ocean without punishment or sword, but through righteousness, he dwells therein.
“But if he goes forth from the home life into homelessness, he becomes an Arahant, a perfectly enlightened Buddha who draws back the veil from the world.
“But where, Master Keṇiya, does that venerable Gotama, the Arahant, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, dwell at present?
When this was said, Keṇiya the coiled-hair ascetic raised his right arm and said this to the brahmin Sela:
“That, Master Sela, is a row of blue forest trees.
Then the brahmin Sela, together with three hundred young brahmin students, approached the Blessed One.
Thereupon, the brahmin Sela addressed those young brahmin students:
“Come, sirs, with little noise, placing one foot down after the other;
for those Blessed Ones are difficult to approach, wandering alone like lions.
And when I am conversing with the ascetic Gotama, do not, sirs, interrupt my speech midway.”
“May your honors wait until the conclusion of my discourse.
Then the brahmin Sela approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.
When they had concluded their polite and courteous conversation, he sat down to one side.
As he was sitting to one side, the brahmin Sela examined the Blessed One’s body for the thirty-two marks of a Great Man.
The brahmin Sela saw the thirty-two marks of a Great Man on the Blessed One’s body, with the exception of two.
Regarding those two marks of a Great Man, he was hesitant, doubtful, undecided, and lacked confidence.
And his private parts were concealed in a sheath, and he possessed a long tongue.
Then it occurred to the Blessed One:
“This brahmin Sela perceives my thirty-two marks of a Great Man, with the exception of two.”
“He is doubtful, uncertain, undecided, and lacks confidence regarding two marks of a Great Man:
his male organ being sheathed and his tongue being large.
Then the Blessed One performed such a feat of psychic power that the brahmin Sela saw the Blessed One’s male organ was sheathed.
Then the Blessed One, having extended his tongue, touched and stroked both ear canals; he touched and stroked both nostrils; and he covered his entire forehead with his tongue.
Then it occurred to the brahmin Sela:
"The ascetic Gotama is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, complete and not incomplete."
Yet I do not know for certain whether he is a Buddha or not.
However, I have heard this from aged and elderly brahmins, the teachers of teachers, as they were speaking:
"Those who are Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, reveal themselves when their own praise is being spoken."
“What if I were to praise the ascetic Gotama to his face with appropriate verses?
Then the brahmin Sela praised the Blessed One to his face with appropriate verses:
“With a perfect body and radiant beauty, You are like a mountain peak, O bull among men.”
Well-born and beautiful to behold,
O Blessed One, you possess a golden complexion and very white teeth, and you are endowed with vigor.
For all those auspicious marks that belong to a well-born man,
they are all present upon your body.
He possesses the marks of a Great Man:
clear-eyed, with a beautiful face, tall,
straight, and majestic.
In the midst of the community of recluses,
you shine like the sun;
you are a bhikkhu of beautiful appearance.
Your skin resembles gold;
what use have you for the state of a recluse,
since you possess such a supreme complexion?
O King, you are worthy to become a wheel-turning monarch, a bull among charioteers,
a conqueror of the four quarters.
Lord of the Jambusaṇḍa:
let the kṣatriyas, the wealthy kings, be your followers.
“O King of kings, lord of men,
rule the kingdom, Gotama!
“I am a king, O Sela,” he said.
I am the unsurpassed King of Dhamma;
by means of the Dhamma I turn the wheel,
a wheel that cannot be turned back.
“You claim to be a perfectly awakened one,
an unsurpassed King of Dhamma:
‘I turn the wheel by means of the Dhamma.’”
Thus you speak, Gotama.
Who indeed is your general,
the disciple who follows in the Teacher's footsteps?
“Who now follows after you,
who sets in motion the Wheel of Dhamma?
“The Wheel set in motion by me— ”
(The Blessed One said:
"Sāriputta turns the unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma in accordance with it."
He has followed the Tathāgata:
that which is to be directly known has been directly known,
and that which is to be developed has been developed.
What was to be abandoned has been abandoned by me;
therefore, O brahmin, I am a Buddha.
Let you dispel your doubt regarding me.
Have faith, O brahmin;
for the frequent sight of the Perfectly Awakened Ones is difficult to obtain.
O Brahmin, I am that fully enlightened one whose appearance in this world is indeed difficult to encounter even frequently.
The unsurpassed surgeon,
become as Brahmā, the incomparable,
the crusher of Māra’s army.
“Having brought all my friends under my control,
I rejoice, free from fear from any quarter.
“Gentlemen, listen to this!
As one with clear vision shines forth,
so does the Great Hero, the surgeon,
roar like a lion in the forest.
Who, having seen him who has become Brahma, who is beyond compare,
the crusher of Māra’s army,
would not have faith?
Even one of dark birth:
let him who wishes follow me,
or let him who does not wish go.
“Here I shall go forth into homelessness in the presence of the one of excellent wisdom.
“If this is pleasing to you, sir— ”
The teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One;
we too shall go forth into homelessness in the presence of him of supreme wisdom.”
These three hundred brahmins,
with palms joined in reverence, entreat you:
"We shall lead the holy life."
“The Blessed One [has taught] the well-expounded holy life in your presence. (The Blessed One said: “The holy life is well-expounded. (Selā)
Visible here and now, not subject to time;
wherein renunciation is not in vain for one who trains with diligence.
The brahmin Sela, together with his retinue, received the going-forth in the presence of the Blessed One and received full ordination.
Then, at the end of that night, Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic had various kinds of fine food, both hard and soft, prepared in his own hermitage and had the time announced to the Blessed One, saying:
"It is time, Master Gotama; the meal is ready."

Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, approached the hermitage of Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic; having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of monks.
Then Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic, with his own hands, personally served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft foods.
When the Blessed One had finished eating and had withdrawn his hand from the bowl, Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic took a certain low seat and sat down to one side.
As Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic sat to one side, the Blessed One expressed his approval with these verses:
“Sacrifices have the fire-oblation as their chief;
the Sāvitrī is the chief of Vedic meters;”
The king is the mouth of men;
the ocean is the mouth of rivers;
the moon is the mouth of the stars.
The sun is the chief of those that give heat;
the Saṅgha is indeed the chief of those who sacrifice, for those desiring merit.
Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to Keṇiya the matted-hair ascetic with these verses,
rose from his seat and departed. Then the Venerable Sela, together with his company, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute,
in no long time attained that supreme goal for which noble sons rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness— the consummation of the holy life.
Having realized it for himself through direct knowledge in this very life, he entered and dwelt therein. He declared:
"Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.
Thus the Venerable Sela, together with his retinue, became an arahant.

Then the Venerable Sela, together with his retinue, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he arranged his robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and addressed the Blessed One in verse:
“Having come for refuge to you, O Seer, eight days ago from now—”
In seven nights, O Blessed One, we have been tamed in your teaching.
You are the Buddha; you are the Teacher.
You are the Sage who has overcome Māra;
having severed the underlying tendencies,
you have crossed over and deliver this generation.
The acquisitions have been transcended by you;
the taints have been shattered by you;
like a lion, you are free from clinging.
These three hundred bhikkhus stand with palms joined in reverence, having abandoned fear and dread.
“Stretch out your feet, O Hero;
let the Nāgas pay homage to the Teacher.
The second Sela Sutta is finished.
